ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-closing screening of every UBO, general partner, limited partner, director, and senior manager against: (i) Canadian Autonomous Sanctions Lists administered under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (ii) Public Safety Canada and RCMP listed terrorist entities; (iii) OFAC SDN List, with attention to U.S. nexus of USD wire transfers and L/C payments; (iv) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (v) global PEP databases and adverse media from recognized providers. Enhanced due diligence mandatory for any PEP, family member, close associate, or any jurisdiction identified as high-risk by FATF. If any screening hit is flagged, the incorporation must be paused and a senior compliance officer must conduct enhanced review; FINTRAC reporting applies for suspicious transaction indicators.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Centrale de recherche et de vérification via the official portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French dominance in the company name under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11). The name must be suitable for use in French; a non-French trademark or corporate name may be tolerated only if no French equivalent exists and it is briefly accompanied by a French descriptor or generic term. Latin transliteration required for non-Latin scripts; accents and punctuation must follow Quebec linguistic and legal publicity guidance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Partnership / Société en commandite (without required structural truthfulness)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives the registar's written decision citing the grounds and the specific provisions of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1). The applicant may file a written application for reconsideration (révision) with the Registrar within 30 days of the decision, attaching supporting evidence (e.g., trademark registration, consent from disciplinary or heritage authority for sensitive words, or cultural justification). If reconsideration fails, judicial review may be filed with the Superior Court of Quebec under article 529 of the Code of Civil Procedure within the applicable prescription period. Name reservation may be renewed by filing a new reservation request before expiry, subject to re-search and availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only when the virtual office provider offers a physical reception desk, dedicated postal address, acceptance of legal service of process, telephone answering with local zone code, and maintenance of records at that address. A Quebec limited partnership must have a declared establishment address in Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A bare mail-forwarding service without physical staff and service-of-process acceptance is not acceptable. For UHT oat milk plant operations, a virtual office cannot substitute for the manufacturing facility address, which must be registered separately as an actual place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard manufacturing facility in the food and beverage sector; estimated annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the Registraire des entreprises or provincial food inspection authority is below 10% absent red flags, but rises to greater than 40% if regulatory complaints, UBO inaccuracies, auxiliary mail-only registered office, or sanctions/PEP risk events are present. In addition, municipal zoning, fire safety, and Quebec Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAPAQ) inspections occur with prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236–2250 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 1–31 and regulations; where the general partner is a body corporate, Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises du Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, supplemented by the Déclaration d'établissement (Declaration regarding the place of business).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital may be fixed in cash, equipment or industrial assets (UHT line). CCQ arts. 2245 and 2249 prohibit limited partners from withdrawing contributions where the withdrawal would reduce the partnership's assets below the capital figure declared in the Declaration of Registration or render the partnership insolvent. No escrow account or bank block is required by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Limited Partnership hereby adopts the limited partnership agreement and the Declaration of Registration for the aseptic barista-formula hydrolyzed oat milk UHT plant and packaging business (ISIC 1050) in Québec. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the General Partner subscribes to its general partner capital contribution and accepts the capital subscriptions of the limited partners as recorded in the Declaration of Registration. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership is established at [UHT Plant Site], Québec, which is designated as the principal establishment for legal publicity. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Operating Officer of the Partnership and authorized signing officers for filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec are confirmed, effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Clearance with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online reservation portal (RegistreEntreprise website) or head-office in Montréal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the REQ portal with a verifiable legal entity login or file a paper 'Demande de réservation de nom' through an authorized representative. Reserve the exact business name, including the mandatory legal element 'S.E.C.' (société en commandite) or 'Limited Partnership / L.P.' if English, and the municipality of the UHT plant. Provide the general partner's identification and a precise statement of the object (ISIC 1050 — manufacture of aseptic barista oat milk and packaging). Save the reservation number assigned by REQ.
required_dossiers: Completed 'Demande de réservation de nom' form
Notarized power of attorney or mandate for the representative (if the signatory is not an authorized officer)
Identification of the general partner (passport or provincial ID / SIN where requested)
Municipal address and legal posting address of the future principal establishment
Payment instrument for the approx. CAD 42 fee (cards or Swift/TT if foreign)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit with a distinctive variation (geographic or commercial qualifier) or address the REQ name-review committee; if REQ issues a correction notice, answer in writing within 45 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or attorney advising the general partner, and REQ form-preparation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement (convention de société en commandite), specifying the capital contributions of the general and limited partners, the conduct of business for the UHT oat milk plant, income/loss allocation, right of first refusal, and management authority of the general partner. Have the general partner (and limited partners, if named in the declaration) execute the Declaration of Registration. Where any capital contribution is made in real estate or an industrial lease is granted, execute before a notary; otherwise a private writing is valid. Obtain the general partner's corporate board resolution if the GP is a corporation.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Déclaration d'immatriculation (REQ form, pre-filled with reservation number)
Declaration regarding the place of business (Déclaration d'établissement) for the plant address and for head office
Resolution of the general partner dated to the same day as execution
Confirmatory notarized signature page (in the session of the notary) when requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the document is refused for lacking notarization, complete the missing notarial certification within the 90-day REQ deferral and resubmit; if the declarations contain errors, correct them before filing to avoid penalties under ALPE s. 20.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration and Fee Settlement; Issuance of NEQ and Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online 'Mon dossier entreprise' / 'Espace entreprise' filing centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the declaration and supplementary documents via the REQ portal; pay the registration fee (approx. CAD 84 total, name reservation and registration) using a card or institutional wire. After electronic validation, download the 'Certificat d'immatriculation' bearing the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and the public registry extract. Cross-check that the partnership description, the commercial object, and the designated establishment are correct.
required_dossiers: Signed declaration of registration
Certificate of name reservation
Proof of fee payment / wire receipt
Original mandate (if filed through a lawyer or accountant)
Identification of the establishment address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected or suspended, respond to the REQ 'avis' via the online follow-up and supply the corrected declaration or notarized signatures; if the certificate has errors, proceed with a rectifying declaration (no new fee) or file before the publicity judge to force registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Tax Registration — Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration online; Revenu Québec (RQ) Business Registration (Clé / RQ sign in)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register the partnership for the federal Business Number (BN) and then open the RQ file for the QST (TVQ), GST, and payroll source deductions (if the LP will hire production workers). As the LP is fiscally transparent, the general partner files the registrations in the partnership's name; enter the UHT plant address as the 'establishment in Canada' and designate the general partner as the authorized person. Keep the Swift LC or wire banking details in the RQ/CRA files for refunds.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (NEQ)
Limited partnership agreement (copy)
CRA BN application RP-1 / RQ application form (online equivalent)
General partner's SIN or corporate BN
Plant site lease or proof of municipal occupancy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrations are queried, file corrected applications through the RQ 'espace professional' and provide the GP resolution; appeal any denied QST registration to the service de la vérification within 90 days; if the partnership is classified 'non-resident' for the federal GST, adjust the general partner's address file before the CRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CNESST Employer Registration and Mandatory Occupational Health & Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) — Business Services / Espace employer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LP as an employer within 60 days of first hiring; open the workers' compensation insurance account under the NAICS 311999 unit (miscellaneous food manufacturing) and submit the salary estimation. Adopt and post the workplace prevention program covering the UHT line, CIP chemical handling, aseptic steam/heat and lockout/tagout; request the attendant workplace clearance and book the mandatory fire/evacuation training with the local municipal fire department.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate
CNESST employer registration declaration
Prevention program (programme de prévention)
Staffing and payroll list by job classification
Municipal occupancy/operating permits (zoning, fire) or application evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CNESST classifies the plant under a higher-risk unit, the employer may object within 30 days of the notice of classification; if the clearance is conditional, complete the machine-guarding and fire safety corrective actions and request a re-inspection; appeal any contested decision to the Tribunal administratif du travail (TAT) within 45 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) — Food Inspection Division, in coordination with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) Safe Food for Canadians licensing office, and the municipal building/public works department at the plant site
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: MAPAQ Food Establishment Permit (permis d'établissement alimentaire) and CFIA Safe Food for Canadians (SFCR) Processing Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale, with the municipal sewer authority of the plant site
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Certificate of authorization ('certificat d'autorisation') under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2); a full EIA report is not triggered for UHT oat milk processing unless the plant is located in a sensitive area (wetland, floodplain) or exceeds waste-generation thresholds; generally an industrial registration and a municipal sewer discharge permit suffice.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6.5–9.5, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L, fats/oils/grease ≤ 50 mg/L at the industrial sewer connection, per municipal pre-treatment by-law and the Quebec sewage disposal regulation. Air: compliance with the Regulation respecting the atmosphere — boiler opacity ≤ 20%, NOx/SO2 limits for natural-gas boilers, and catalytic/thermal oxidizer VOC removal efficiency ≥ 95% for any aseptic packaging adhesive/solvent line. Refrigerants: CFC-free (R-134a/R-290 compliant). Waste: mandatory diversion/recycling of oat hulls, cardboard, and HDPE/UHT carton gable trim under the Regulation respecting residual materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire prevention service (per the Quebec Fire Safety Code, c. B-1.1, r. 1) covering UHT tanks, the aseptic packaging hall, and ammonia/glycol cold rooms; structural load inspection certificate for the silo area and packaging mezzanine issued by a licensed engineer (Engineers Act, c. I-9) and filed with the municipal building department; occupational workplace clearance certificate from CNESST for the implementation of the prevention program, machine-guarding of the UHT homogenizers and CIP systems, lockout/tagout, and ergonomic load-station requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year, between January 1 and May 31 (inclusive).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee of CAD 42 if filed after May 31; continued non-filing triggers a 30-day notice of striking-off (déchéance) and eventual cancellation of the limited partnership's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal income tax information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, due March 31 of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal period end, due within 90 days after the end of the fiscal period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA may assess late-filing penalties under the Income Tax Act for each overdue day, plus interest; repeated or grossly negligent non-filing may expose the general partners to additional penalties and prosecution under section 238.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-871 Partnership Income Tax Information Return (Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, due March 31 of the following calendar year; for any other fiscal period end, due within the same 90-day filing window prescribed for the federal T5013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec can assess late-filing penalties and interest on unpaid amounts; the general partners are jointly and severally liable for the penalties incurred by the partnership for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit applies to a Quebec limited partnership solely because of its legal form. A certified audit may become required via the limited partnership agreement, a lender covenant, a securities regulatory order, or if the partnership is subject to a specific provincial or federal licensing regime for the food manufacturing industry.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for public accountable enterprises; ASPE for private entities and limited partnerships unless the partners or a regulator require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a Quebec limited partnership, the annual REQ declaration serves as the annual UBO confirmation. Any transfer of a partnership interest, change in general partners, or change in a limited partner's contribution must be reported to the REQ within 30 days; annual filing must reflect all partners holding a controlling or significant economic interest as of the declaration date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and Partnership Resolutions Record

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 - CAD 600 per annum (USD 185 - USD 445) for registered office and agent services in Quebec.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 7,000 - CAD 15,000 per annum (USD 5,200 - USD 11,100) if a certified audit is contractually required; no mandatory audit fee otherwise.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Entity level: 0% (Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent; income flows through to partners). Partner level: combined federal (15%) + Quebec (11.5%) general corporate rate = 26.5% for corporate partners; top combined federal/Quebec marginal rate for individual partners = 53.31%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC partners may claim the federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal on first CAD 500,000) plus Quebec's reduced SME rate (3.2%), producing a combined 12.2% effective rate on qualifying active business income; federal Manufacturing and Processing profits reduction (13% federal for CCPCs on M&P income not eligible for SBD); federal SR&ED refundable ITC of 33.33% for CCPCs and Quebec SR&ED credit up to 30% for manufacturing SMEs; 10-year Quebec tax holiday for large manufacturing investments (CAD 100M+) in qualifying regions; accelerated capital cost allowance for clean-energy equipment used in UHT processing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) filed via CRA e-services / eT5013 EFILE; with T5013 slips issued to each partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than the earliest income tax return filing deadline of any partner: April 30 (individuals), June 15 (self-employed individuals), or 6 months after corporate partner's taxation year-end (June 30 for a December 31 year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, business number (BN), province/state of formation, and head office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide foreign tax identification number and country of residence; the LP must have a Canadian BN even if all partners are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the partnership's fiscal period (YYYYMMDD).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fiscal period is set under ITA s. 249.1 and must be coordinated with partners' taxation years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss of the partnership computed on a CRA tax basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reported at partnership level; allocation schedule assigns each non-resident partner's share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Active business income or loss from the UHT aseptic oat milk plant and packaging operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Active business income of a non-resident partner is taxed on a net basis under Part I (DTA business profits article); no gross-basis Part XIII WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's allocable share of business income/loss, taxable capital gains, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocation must follow the LP agreement and reflect real economic entitlement; allocations must be reported in the currency of the LP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies treaty-resident partners and their country of residence for reduced withholding or Part I relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim treaty protection via Schedule 10; certificates of residence (TRC) must be produced on CRA request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013: CAD 25/day, min CAD 100, max CAD 2,500 per return (CAD 7,500 for partnerships with 51+ partners); failure to issue T5013 slips: CAD 100 per slip up to CAD 7,500; false statement penalty CAD 100 per false statement; partner-level late filing 5% + 1%/month (max 12 months) and gross negligence 50% penalty on understatement.
